title: Japan's low-leverage economy should withstand rate hikes
gist: Oxford Economics expects BoJ rate hikes over coming months to be absorbed by Japan's low-leverage firms and net-saver households, with vulnerabilities in small firms and 30-40s mortgage borrowers, and sees room for the BoJ to go beyond 1.75% subject to government pushback.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects the Bank of Japan's coming rate hikes to leave Japan on a modest but steady growth path because most firms and households have healthy balance sheets.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Japanese growth is not seen as a constraint on further BoJ tightening.
insights.locator: The rate hikes we expect over the next few months

insights.claim: Most Japanese companies should keep a reasonable spread between return on assets and interest costs thanks to low leverage and rising profitability.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Corporate credit risk from higher rates looks contained for the aggregate.
insights.locator: Most companies will likely maintain a reasonable spread

insights.claim: A 1ppt rise in effective interest rates could lift the share of loss-making small Japanese firms from 27% to 31%.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Small-cap and SME credit is the transmission point for BoJ-hike stress.
insights.locator: an analysis of small firms shows

insights.claim: Japanese households are net savers so hikes raise deposit income overall, but people in their 30s and 40s are net debtors on overwhelmingly floating-rate mortgages, weakening already stagnant residential investment with limited overall growth impact.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Housing and younger-cohort consumption bear the burden while aggregate demand is cushioned.
insights.locator: On aggregate, the Japanese are net savers

insights.claim: The economy's resilience may let the BoJ hike beyond 1.75% to prevent further yen weakness or de-anchoring of inflation expectations from prolonged cost-push inflation, but damage to vulnerable small firms and households could make the government more cautious and pressure the bank.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Terminal-rate risk skews up on the yen, but political pressure is the offsetting constraint to watch.
insights.locator: may allow the Bank of Japan to hike its policy rate beyond 1.75%
